title: Discount code usable one time more than max_uses
explanation: The used-up check is `times_used > max_uses`, so when times_used == max_uses the code is still accepted and times_used becomes max_uses + 1. The docstring says max_uses is the total number of orders that may use the code; the comparison must be `>=`.

title: Discount truncates instead of rounding to the nearest cent, via float math
explanation: `int(price_cents * (100 - percent_off) / 100)` goes through a float and truncates toward zero, while the docstring promises rounding to the nearest cent. E.g. apply_discount(3333, 10) returns 2999 instead of 3000 and apply_discount(2995, 15) returns 2545 instead of 2546, so customers are systematically under-charged by up to a cent per seat. Money in integer cents should use integer arithmetic with explicit rounding (e.g. (price * (100 - pct) + 50) // 100).

title: Ticket codes generated with non-cryptographic random
explanation: Ticket codes are bearer credentials (the gate admits whoever presents a valid code) but are produced with `random.choices`, a Mersenne Twister PRNG whose output can be predicted after observing enough codes. An attacker who buys a few tickets could forge valid codes for other seats. Use `secrets.choice`/`secrets.token_*`. There is also no uniqueness check against already issued codes.

title: Discount use is consumed even when checkout then fails
explanation: `self.discounts.redeem(...)` increments times_used before the tickets are priced. If `tier_for_seat` raises PricingError for a seat whose row no tier covers (or any later step fails), the order is never created but the limited-use code has already been counted, so a failed checkout burns one of the code's uses. Redeem only after all seats have been priced successfully (or validate first and count the use at the end).

title: Checkout accepts empty holds and events that already started
explanation: Nothing prevents a hold with zero seats (SeatMap.hold accepts an empty list), so checkout creates an order with no tickets that still charges the booking fee. Neither hold() nor checkout() checks `now` against `event.starts_at`, so tickets can be sold for an event that is already over, and such tickets are immediately past the refund deadline.

title: hold() does not reject an empty seat list
explanation: With `seats=[]` the missing list is empty and a hold covering no seats is created and returned; checkout of that hold produces an order of zero tickets charged the booking fee. The method should require at least one seat.

title: Order ids derived from dict length and not unique across offices
explanation: `ORD-{len(self.orders) + 1}` assumes orders are never removed (any removal yields a duplicate id that silently overwrites an existing order) and every TicketOffice restarts at ORD-00001, so ids collide as soon as orders of several events are combined, e.g. in export_orders_csv. Ids are also sequential and guessable, which matters because refund_ticket authorises by order id + ticket code only. Use a dedicated counter or a UUID.

title: Circular import between purchase and refunds
explanation: purchase.py imports refunds (line 10, for refund_deadline) and refunds.py imports purchase (for the TicketOffice type). It only works because refunds uses purchase in annotations under `from __future__ import annotations` and Python falls back to the partially initialised module; any module-level use will raise ImportError. The refund policy (refund_deadline) belongs in a module that does not depend on the office, or the TicketOffice type should be imported under TYPE_CHECKING.

title: Refund has no customer authorisation
explanation: refund_ticket takes only order id and ticket code; it never checks that the caller is the order's customer. Order ids are sequential (ORD-00001, ...) and ticket codes are predictable (random module), so anyone who learns or guesses a code can refund someone else's ticket and put the seat back on sale.

title: Cancelling an event puts its seats back on sale
explanation: cancel_event calls `office.seat_map.release_sold` for every refunded ticket but never marks the event or office as cancelled, so all seats become available again and hold()/checkout() will happily sell tickets for the cancelled event. Also the `order.event_id == office.event.event_id` check is redundant (an office only sells one event) and the if/else accumulation can be a dict.get.

title: Revenue uses the tier price instead of what was paid
explanation: The docstring and README say revenue is what customers actually paid after discounts, but the code adds `ticket.base_price_cents`. Every discounted sale is over-reported in the sales report; it must add `ticket.paid_cents`.

title: CSV formula injection through customer names
explanation: The customer string is written verbatim into orders.csv. A customer name starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is executed as a formula when the export is opened in Excel/LibreOffice (CSV injection). Customer-controlled cells should be escaped (e.g. prefix with a quote) before export.

title: Duplicated CSV export logic
explanation: export_sales_csv and export_orders_csv repeat the same buffer/encode/write/checksum sequence with only header, rows and file name differing. A shared helper taking (name, header, rows) removes the duplication so a fix (atomic write, escaping, directory creation) only has to be made once.
